governance_posts.title: Aave DeFi Watcher – Browser Extension for Monitoring Aave Positions
governance_posts.description:
Hi dear aave community :)

I’d like to share Aave DeFi Watcher, a browser extension I built to make monitoring Aave positions simple, fast, and privacy-friendly.

I originally started building it because the previously shared Aave Monitor extension appears to no longer function reliably. For example, many addresses currently return “Failed to fetch” instead of account data. It also only supports Aave V3, while I wanted a tool that could monitor positions across Aave V2, V3, and V4. Since I needed a working solution myself, I decided to build one from scratch.

Features

  • Total Collateral
  • Total Debt
  • Available to Borrow
  • Loan-to-Value (LTV)
  • Liquidation Threshold
  • Health Factor
  • Monitor multiple wallet addresses
  • Support for Aave V2, V3, and V4
  • Support for multiple networks including Ethereum, Arbitrum, Optimism, Base, Polygon, and Avalanche
  • Desktop notifications for Health Factor alerts
  • Privacy Mode to hide balances while continuing to monitor your positions
  • Automatic RPC fallback for improved reliability

One of my favorite features is the extension badge, which displays the Health Factor of your selected address directly on the browser toolbar, allowing you to monitor your position at a glance.

The extension is completely read-only. It never asks you to connect a wallet or sign transactions. All account data is fetched directly from Aave’s public smart contracts.

Chrome Web Store

chromewebstore.google.com

Aave DeFi Watcher - Chrome Web Store

Monitor your Aave health factor and liquidation risk in real time across chains.

I built this extension for my own daily use and decided to share it with the community. It’s actively maintained, and I plan to continue adding new features and supporting future Aave releases.

I’d really appreciate any feedback, bug reports or feature suggestions from the community :))

governance_posts.title: Risk Stewards: Cap and IRM Changes on Aave V3 / 2026.10.29
governance_posts.description:
Summary

LlamaRisk recommends the following parameter changes based on user behavior, on-chain liquidity, and position health observed in the latest review of Aave V3 reserves.

Aave V3 Core:

  • Increase optimalUsageRatio for USDT from 92.00% to 94.00%.

Aave V3 Base:

  • Increase supply cap for cbETH from 60,000 to 70,000.

Aave V3 Avalanche:

  • Reduce supply cap for WAVAX from 16,000,000 to 14,000,000.

Aave V3 Arbitrum:

  • Increase Slope1 for USDC from 4.10% to 4.20%.

Aave V3 X Layer:

  • Reduce supply cap for PT-USDG-29OCT2026 from 50,000,000 to 1.
  • Reduce supply cap for USDe from 100,000,000 to 25,000,000.
  • Reduce borrow cap for USDe from 20,000,000 to 10,000,000.

cbETH (Aave V3 Base)

cbETH has reached 94.0% supply cap utilization (56,378 / 60,000) on the Aave V3 Base instance, with supply up 22.3% over the past 30 days.

cbETH Supply Distribution


Source: LlamaRisk, October 29, 2026

All of the top twenty cbETH suppliers carry debt, at health factors between 1.02 and 15.30 with a median of 1.18, and supply is concentrated, with the largest supplier holding approximately 34% and the top three approximately 77%. Eleven borrow WETH against cbETH, which accounts for nearly all of the cohort’s debt, and ten hold smaller USDC borrowings, so HF for most of the debt depends on the cbETH-versus-ETH spread.

Recommendation

We recommend raising the supply cap from 60,000 to 70,000 on Aave V3 Base, landing at approximately 80.5% post-change cap utilization.

Cap Reductions

  • WAVAX on Aave V3 Avalanche sits at 101.9% supply cap utilization (16,298,323 / 16,000,000), with supply down 7.3% over the past 30 days. The proposed cap of 14,000,000 sits below current outstanding supply (approximately 116.4% post-change cap utilization), which limits further growth in WAVAX collateral while DEX liquidity for WAVAX on Avalanche remains limited.
  • USDe on Aave V3 X Layer sits at 2.7% supply cap utilization (2,746,676 / 100,000,000) with no outstanding debt against a 20,000,000 borrow cap. The proposed supply cap of 25,000,000 is approximately 9.1x current outstanding supply, landing at approximately 11.0% post-change cap utilization, and the borrow cap moves from 20,000,000 to 10,000,000.

Matured PTs

  • PT-USDG-29OCT2026 on Aave V3 X Layer reached its scheduled maturity on October 29, 2026. The reserve holds approximately 5,591,013 PT against a 50,000,000 supply cap, with supply down 91.6% over the past 30 days ahead of maturity. After maturity, the PT becomes redeemable at par against the underlying. The proposed supply cap of 1 closes new deposits while existing holders retain the ability to withdraw or redeem.

USDC Slope1 Increase (Aave V3 Arbitrum)

USDC on Aave V3 Arbitrum holds approximately 218.8M USDC of supply against 168.3M of debt, at 76.9% utilization against a 90% optimal utilization point. Over the past 30 days, supply grew 21.4% while debt grew 6.4%, bringing utilization down from 87.8%.

The recommendation raises Slope1 by 10 BPS, from 4.10% to 4.20%. The base rate, Slope2, and the optimal utilization point are unchanged, so the borrow rate at the optimal point moves from 4.10% to 4.20% APR and the rate at full utilization from 14.10% to 14.20% APR.

Instance Asset Utilization uOptimal Current Borrow APR New Borrow APR Delta
Aave V3 Arbitrum USDC 76.9% 90.0% 3.50% 3.59% +9 BPS

USDC on Aave V3 Arbitrum carries a lower Slope1 than the 4.50% applied to most stablecoin reserves across Aave V3, including USD₮0 on the same instance. We plan to continue raising Slope1 toward 4.50% gradually, in incremental steps, with the size and timing of each step set by observed borrow demand, utilization, and broader market conditions.

USDT Optimal Utilization (Aave V3 Core)

USDT on Aave V3 Core holds approximately 2.7B USDT of supply against 2.5B of debt, at 92.9% utilization, above the current 92.00% optimal point. The blue-chip collateral LTV increase on Aave V3 Core (WETH, WBTC, cbBTC, wstETH and weETH) executed on October 28, 2026, and the recommendation returns the optimal utilization point to 94.00%. The base rate, Slope1, and Slope2 are unchanged, so the borrow rate at the optimal point stays at 4.50% APR and the rate at full utilization stays at 14.50% APR.

At the current 92.9% utilization, the reserve moves from the Slope2 segment back onto Slope1: the variable borrow rate would move from 5.56% to 4.45% APR, and the supply rate from 4.65% to 3.71% APR.

Withdrawal Liquidity at the Optimal Point

The optimal point sets how much of the supply remains available for withdrawal when the reserve operates at its intended level. Moving it up by two percentage points converts approximately 54.0M USDT of withdrawal buffer into borrow capacity priced on Slope1.

The largest USDT supplier holds approximately 186.8M (6.9% of supply), and the five largest approximately 543.2M (20.1%). The largest position sits below the 216.0M withdrawal buffer at the current optimal point and above the 162.0M buffer at the new one, so supplier concentration against the exit buffer warrants monitoring. title: [Direct-To-AIP] Onboard PT-sUSDe-28JAN2027 to Aave V3 Plasma Instance

author: @TokenLogic

created: 2026-10-21

Summary

This proposal seeks to list PT-sUSDe-28JAN2027 on Aave V3 Plasma through the Direct-to-AIP process, providing a rollover destination for users of PT-sUSDe-22OCT2026 ahead of its maturity on 22 October 2026.

Motivation

PT-sUSDe-22OCT2026 matures on 22 October 2026, with approximately 20.72M PT supplied to Aave V3 Plasma as of 21 October. The proposed January listing would allow holders to roll into the next maturity and continue using PT-sUSDe as collateral on the instance.

The rollover follows the established sequence of sUSDe PT listings on Plasma, covering the January, April, June and October 2026 maturities.

At the time of writing, the January PT has approximately 99 days remaining until maturity, compared with approximately 132 days when the October PT was assessed. The shorter remaining term reduces the PT’s price sensitivity to changes in implied yield, supporting the case for risk parameters at least in line with the October listing, subject to Risk Service Providers’ assessment of liquidity and liquidation conditions.

Risk Service Providers will recommend the supply cap, oracle configuration and dedicated E-Mode categories for PT-sUSDe-28JAN2027 and sUSDe collateral against stablecoin borrowing. These recommendations will be incorporated into the AIP before the vote.

governance_posts.title: Risk Stewards: Supply and Borrow Cap Changes on Aave V3 / 2026.10.16
governance_posts.description:
Summary

LlamaRisk recommends the following parameter changes based on user behavior, position health, and borrow cap headroom observed in the latest review of Aave V3 reserves.

Aave V3 Prime:

  • Increase supply cap for tETH from 15,000 to 20,000.

Aave V3 Core:

  • Reduce supply cap for tETH from 300 to 1.
  • Reduce borrow cap for WBTC from 4,000 to 1,500.
  • Reduce borrow cap for cbBTC from 1,440 to 500.

Aave V3 Arbitrum:

  • Reduce borrow cap for WETH from 135,000 to 75,000.

tETH (Aave V3 Prime and Aave V3 Core)

tETH is listed on both Aave V3 Prime and Aave V3 Core, and on both instances, it counts as collateral only within E-Mode. On Aave V3 Prime, the reserve holds 15,189 tETH (approximately USD 46.9M) against a 15,000 supply cap (101.3% utilization). On Aave V3 Core, supply has remained between approximately 90 and 300 tETH since late April and stands at 286.78 tETH (approximately USD 0.9M), about 1.9% of the Prime figure.

Supply Distribution (Aave V3 Prime)


Source: LlamaRisk, October 16, 2026

The top tETH suppliers have health factors between 1.02 and 1.07 with a median of 1.05, all carry outstanding debt, and supply is highly concentrated, with the largest position accounting for 77.5% of the reserve. Every position borrows wstETH against tETH collateral within the tETH/wstETH E-Mode category, so the health factor of the cohort tracks the tETH/wstETH exchange rate.

Recommendation

Adoption of tETH on Aave V3 Core has remained low, while demand for the asset sits on Aave V3 Prime, where it is paired with wstETH debt in a dedicated E-Mode category. We recommend reducing the supply cap on Aave V3 Core from 300 to 1, which stops new deposits on that instance without affecting existing positions, and raising the supply cap on Aave V3 Prime from 15,000 to 20,000, which places the reserve at approximately 75.9% post-change cap utilization.

Borrow Cap Reductions

  • WBTC on Aave V3 Core carries 700 WBTC of debt (approximately USD 57.3M) against a 4,000 borrow cap (17.5% utilization), with borrows down 10.4% over the past 30 days. The proposed borrow cap of 1,500 lands at approximately 46.7% post-change borrow cap utilization, aligning the cap with observed demand while retaining headroom.
  • cbBTC on Aave V3 Core carries 128 cbBTC of debt (approximately USD 10.5M) against a 1,440 borrow cap (8.9% utilization), with borrows up 24.8% over the past seven days. The proposed borrow cap of 500 lands at approximately 25.7% post-change borrow cap utilization, retaining ample room for further growth.
  • WETH on Aave V3 Arbitrum carries 55,461 WETH of debt (approximately USD 136.0M) against a 135,000 borrow cap (41.1% utilization), with borrows broadly unchanged over the past 30 days. The proposed borrow cap of 75,000 lands at approximately 73.9% post-change borrow cap utilization, aligning the cap with observed demand.

Specification

Aave V3 Prime tETH 15,000 20,000
Aave V3 Core tETH 300 1

Borrow Caps

Aave V3 Arbitrum WETH 135,000 75,000

governance_posts.title: tBTC Mint & Redeem Pause: Aave's Response
governance_posts.description:
Last updated 10:26 UTC, 31 October 2026.

What happened

On 31 October 2026, Threshold Network issued a pre-emptive pause of tBTC mints & redeems. We are in communication with the Threshold team and are closely monitoring their updates.

tBTC is listed on Aave V3 on Ethereum Core, Base, and Arbitrum. The Base and Arbitrum reserves were previously frozen in earlier asset deprecation rounds, making Ethereum Core the only market where tBTC could still support new borrowing.

What we did

We recommended a pre-emptive freeze of tBTC on Aave V3 Ethereum Core. The aim is to prevent Aave’s exposure to tBTC from growing while the pause is in place by stopping new borrowing against tBTC and new tBTC deposits until the incident is confirmed to be fully mitigated by Threshold. We prepared the freeze transaction and proposed it to the guardian multisig, which executed it at 10:01 UTC.

A freeze stops new tBTC deposits and stops tBTC from adding borrowing power to any position. Users can still repay and withdraw; liquidations continue to run; and borrowing against other collateral works as normal. tBTC keeps its liquidation threshold, so the health factors of existing positions do not change and no position becomes liquidatable due to the freeze. Frozen reserves accept no new supply, so while the freeze is on, users can raise their health factor by repaying debt or adding additional collateral.

The freeze applies only to tBTC on Ethereum Core. No other reserve is affected, and no market has been paused.

Next steps

We will continue to follow Threshold’s updates and monitor tBTC positions on Aave and tBTC liquidity on secondary markets. Once we have assurance that tBTC operations return to normal, we will propose restorative measures, and we will share that update in this thread.

Users can still repay and withdraw; liquidations continue to run; and borrowing against other collateral works as normal. tBTC keeps its liquidation threshold, so the health factors of existing positions do not change and no position becomes liquidatable due to the freeze. Frozen reserves accept no new supply, so while the freeze is on, users can raise their health factor by repaying debt or adding additional collateral.

The freeze applies only to tBTC on Ethereum Core. No other reserve is affected, and no market has been paused.

Next steps

We will continue to follow Threshold’s updates and monitor tBTC positions on Aave and tBTC liquidity on secondary markets. Once we have assurance that tBTC operations return to normal, we will propose restorative measures, and we will share that update in this thread.

governance_posts.title: Temp Check / Discussion: Exploration of Aave Deployment on Cardano (Feasibility Study Proposal)
governance_posts.description:
Summary

This ARC proposes initiating a structured feasibility study to evaluate the potential deployment of Aave on Cardano.

The objective is to assess:

  • Technical compatibility

  • Risk framework requirements

  • Liquidity and market viability

This is the first step to determine whether further exploration is justified.

Motivation

Aave has successfully expanded across multiple EVM-compatible networks. However, the broader DeFi ecosystem remains concentrated around a single execution paradigm.

At the same time, alternative blockchain architectures have matured. Cardano represents one such environment, characterized by:

  • eUTXO-based transaction model

  • Functional programming approach to smart contracts

  • Emphasis on deterministic execution and formal methods

  • High levels of validator decentralization

Despite these properties, DeFi activity and TVL on Cardano remain relatively limited compared to other ecosystems.

This creates a potential opportunity to evaluate whether:

  • Aave could act as a foundational DeFi primitive in that environment

  • A new user and liquidity segment could be accessed

  • Architectural diversification could provide strategic value

Strategic Considerations

1. Architectural Diversification

Exploring deployment outside the EVM ecosystem may:

  • Reduce reliance on a single execution model

  • Provide exposure to alternative design trade-offs

2. Early Positioning in an Underdeveloped DeFi Market

Cardano currently lacks mature lending infrastructure at scale.
Aave could potentially:

  • Establish early presence

  • Define risk and collateral standards in a new environment

3. Emerging Collateral Opportunities (Forward-Looking)

There is ongoing development in the Cardano ecosystem around non-custodial Bitcoin interoperability, including approaches leveraging Zero-Knowledge technologies.

If successful, this could enable:

  • Use of BTC as collateral without custodial bridges

  • Reduced counterparty risk compared to wrapped assets

While early-stage, this direction may represent a differentiated collateral landscape worth monitoring.

Specification (Feasibility Study Scope)

This ARC proposes conducting a 6–8 week feasibility study covering:

Technical Assessment

  • Mapping Aave architecture to Cardano’s eUTXO model

  • Evaluation of smart contract design constraints

  • Identification of required adaptations or redesigns

Risk & Oracle Framework

  • Oracle availability and reliability

  • Liquidation mechanisms under eUTXO constraints

  • Risk parameter modeling

Market & Liquidity Analysis

  • Current DeFi activity and liquidity depth

  • Potential collateral assets

  • Incentive requirements for market bootstrapping

Ecosystem Dependencies

  • Required infrastructure (indexing, analytics, tooling)

  • Potential collaborators within the Cardano ecosystem

Implementation Considerations

Execution of the feasibility study could be carried out by:

  • Independent contributors

  • Ecosystem-aligned teams

  • External service providers

Subject to community alignment, a follow-up proposal (ARFC) would define:

  • Selected contributors

  • Detailed scope

  • Budget and timeline

Risks

Technical Complexity

  • Fundamental differences between account-based and eUTXO models

  • Potential need for partial or full redesign of components

Liquidity Fragmentation

  • Limited existing DeFi liquidity on Cardano

  • Dependence on incentives and ecosystem coordination

Opportunity Cost

  • Resource allocation vs. expanding within existing EVM ecosystems

Ecosystem Maturity

  • Tooling, oracle infrastructure, and integrations may require additional development

Cost & Funding

This ARC does not request funding.

If the community supports proceeding, a future ARFC would include:

  • A project submission on Project Catalyst to fund the initiative

Next Steps

This ARC seeks feedback from the community on:

  • Whether exploring a non-EVM deployment aligns with Aave’s strategy

  • Whether Cardano is a relevant ecosystem to evaluate

  • Whether the proposed feasibility study scope is appropriate

If there is sufficient support, the next step would be:
→ Drafting an ARFC with defined contributors, scope, and funding requirements.

Conclusion

This proposal does not advocate immediate deployment, but rather a structured evaluation of a potential strategic expansion.

The goal is to determine whether Cardano represents:

  • A viable new market for Aave

  • A meaningful diversification of execution environments

  • A forward-looking opportunity tied to emerging collateral models

Community feedback will determine whether further steps are warranted.

governance_posts.description:
Title: [Direct to AIP] Onboard USAT to Aave V4 Core Instance on Avalanche
Author: @AaveLabs
Date: 2026-10-19

Summary

This proposal seeks to onboard USAT to the Aave V4 Core Instance on Avalanche. This proposal follows the Direct to AIP route.

Motivation

USAT (Tether America USD) is a dollar stablecoin issued by Anchorage Digital Bank, N.A., a federally chartered national trust bank supervised by the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC). USAT is subject to the GENIUS Act and is redeemable 1:1 for U.S. dollars.

Onboarding USAT would:

  • Add a stablecoin issued by a bank under federal supervision in the United States to the Aave V4 Core Instance on Avalanche.
  • Support demand from institutional participants seeking a stablecoin issued under the federal stablecoin framework of the United States.
  • Broaden the range of regulated dollar assets available across Aave deployments.

Specification

This proposal onboards USAT to the Aave V4 Core Instance on Avalanche.

USAT: 0x9A5926fd88F747c357738b1e82aFB46AB80f0A6b

Risk parameters and final configuration will be provided by the Risk Service Providers and this proposal will be updated accordingly.

Useful Links

  • USAT website
  • USAT FAQ

Disclaimer

This proposal was prepared by Aave Labs in its capacity as a contributor to the Aave ecosystem. Aave Labs has no direct financial relationship with Anchorage Digital Bank, N.A., Tether, or their affiliates and has not received compensation from any of these parties in connection with this proposal.

Next Steps

  1. Gather community and Service Provider feedback.
  2. Incorporate the Risk Service Providers’ final configuration for the Aave V4 Core Instance on Avalanche.
  3. Publish the AIP vote for final confirmation and onchain enforcement of the proposal.

governance_posts.title: Introducing AaveAPY: An Yield Dashboard and Simulator
governance_posts.description:
Hi fellow Aave community members,

I am sharing with you an open-source analytics dashboard and simulator that I have been building: AaveAPY.

Live Dashboard: aaveapy.com
Code Source: github.com/0xPabloLI/aaveapy

Key Features

AaveAPY operates as an analytics layer on top of Aave V3.

1. Omni-Chain Yield Comparison

Instead of switching networks, AaveAPY displays a consolidated table showing Native APY + Incentive APY (including points calculator). You can instantly spot the best yield opportunities, filter by asset type, and identify markets with the strongest Supply APY − Borrow APY spread for looping strategies.

2. “What-If” Simulation with On-Chain Protocol Math

Enter a hypothetical supply or borrow amount to simulate the exact impact on your rates. The calculator uses Aave’s native on-chain math (two-slope curve) to show:

  • Supply/borrow APR/APY at the new utilization rate
  • Distance from the optimal utilization (kink) point
  • Remaining borrow cap room and pool liquidity constraints

3. Real Yield After Incentive Caps & Dilution

AaveAPY simulates your actual APY after accounting for incentive caps and dilution, for example:

  • Celo Self-Authentication: Factors in the $1,000 cap per user
  • Merkl/Brevis Forecasts: Estimates the next-run daily rewards and APR for hypothetical deposit amounts based on different campaign type and finite reward pools
  • INK FDV Calculator: Estimate Ink incentive APR based on different Fully Diluted Valuation assumptions

Roadmap

  • Aave V4 protocol support with unified V3/V4 frontend display
  • Complex simulation scenarios across different supply/borrow combinations
  • Smart deployment recommendation with multi-chain yield optimization and cross-chain bridge integration
  • Wallet connection with portfolio import and incentive blacklist/whitelist detection

I built this tool for my own needs, but I hope it brings value to the broader Aave community. Any of your feedback is appreciated.

Enjoy!
